intended_object: The logarithm power series in a topological ring: log x = ∑_{n≥1} (-1)^(n+1)/n · (x-1)^n, i.e. the Mercator series log(1+y) = y − y²/2 + y³/3 − …, evaluated at y = x − 1. It takes the value 0 where the series does not converge. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition picks a ℚ-algebra structure on 𝔸 if one exists. A ring has at most one ℚ-algebra structure, so the choice is canonical. It then takes the sum of `logSeries ℚ 𝔸` at x − 1. The n-th term of `logSeries` is ((-1)^(n+1)/n) • ∏ xᵢ. On the diagonal this gives ((-1)^(n+1)/n) • (x−1)^n. The n = 0 term is 0 because 1/0 = 0 in a field, so it correctly drops out. `FormalMultilinearSeries.sum` is a `tsum`, so the value is 0 when the series is not summable. That matches the documented junk-value convention, and it is the same convention as `NormedSpace.exp`.

If 𝔸 has no ℚ-algebra structure, the coefficients 1/n make no sense, and the junk value 0 is a reasonable choice that the docstring states. The lemma `log_eq_tsum` confirms the intended formula over any characteristic-zero field 𝕂.

The setting is very general: any topological ring, with no norm and no commutativity required. The variable 𝕂 does not enter the definition. So the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no other general logarithm series on topological algebras; `Real.log` and `Complex.log` are specific functions on ℝ and ℂ.
